title: How To Be A Better, Happier Teacher By Slowing Down ing-down/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that constantly rushing through the school day is counterproductive, listing specific ways being in a hurry undermines classroom management: it reduces control, creates restlessness and excitability, diverts attention from students, causes corners to be cut with the classroom management plan, and diminishes teacher leverage. He offers eight concrete tactics to slow down: trimming unnecessary tasks from the day, visualizing the day each morning, waiting until students are fully ready before moving on, enforcing consequences immediately rather than letting them slide to save time, talking less, thoroughly teaching routines and procedures to reduce transition time, observing more, and practicing mindful breathing. The article frames slowing down as a paradoxical time-saver, since misbehavior and disorganization ultimately cost far more time than a deliberate, unhurried pace.
points: Chronic rushing undermines classroom management by increasing restlessness, reducing control, and causing corners to be cut.
Trimming non-essential tasks and visualizing the day each morning are proactive ways to build in more time.
Waiting until every student is fully following along before moving on prevents costly problems later.
Immediately enforcing consequences, rather than letting infractions slide to save time, actually saves time in the long run.
Thoroughly taught routines and procedures reduce the time lost to transitions throughout the day.
quotes: Being in a hurry will make you less effective, not more effective.
All are textbook examples of poor classroom management, and they lead directly to misbehavior, interruptions in learning, and slower academic progress.
Take a close look at everything you do and cut out what isn’t directly related to improving academic progress or classroom management. Focus only on what’s important, and eliminate the rest.

Never move on with a lesson, an activity, or a transition unless you’re getting exactly what you want from your students. Moving on before every student is locked in and following along will come back and bite you later.
When you’re in a hurry, you’ll cut corners—especially with classroom management. But nothing wastes more time than misbehavior. So when a student breaks a rule, enforce it immediately.
Over-explanation is a common mistake teachers make. Get to the point and move on.
Mindful breathing will also protect you from stress, focus your mind, and help you perform at your best.
